steps.body: Check the minute hand first: at 12, it's ":00". Anywhere else, skip-count its position by 5s. Then read the hour from the short hand.
Two clocks: the start is fixed, and the finish moves as time passes. Slide the time forward and watch the finish clock catch up.

widget.prompt: A film starts at 2:15. Set how long it runs so it finishes at 3:00.
widget.successFeedback: 45 minutes — from 2:15, three quarter-hours brings the clock to 3:00.
widget.lowFeedback: Not enough time yet — the finish clock hasn't reached 3:00.
widget.highFeedback: Too much time — the finish clock has run past 3:00.

steps.body: One rule reads every five-minute time: skip-count the minute hand, pair it with the hour.
takeaways: 12 means ":00"; every other position skip-counts the same way.
The short hand always gives the hour.

concept.body: Skip-count the minute hand's clock number by 5s to get the minutes, then pair with the hour from the short hand. Hour between 4 and 5, minute hand at 3: 4:15 (3×5=15).

widget.prompt: The hour hand is between 4 and 5 and the minute hand points to 3. What time is it?
